note: Curated roster of physicians and investigators active in LITT (MRI-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy) and related neurosurgery for neuro-oncology and epilepsy. Coverage is DELIBERATE, not derived from paper authorship — a physician appears here because they are a recognized figure in the field, not because they authored one of the tracked findings. Affiliations were web-verified as of lastUpdated; changing jobs is common, so confidence flags note where a current primary institution could not be confirmed. Each physician's indications map to database.json taxonomy keys, which drives the related-evidence cross-links in the app.

physicians.name: Alexandra J. Golby, MD
physicians.institution: Brigham and Women's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
physicians.littFocus: Senior academic figure in image-guided neurosurgery, intraoperative MRI (AMIGO suite), and brain mapping for tumors and epilepsy near eloquent cortex — a leader in image-guided ablation and resection rather than a single-indication LITT operator.

physicians.name: Gene H. Barnett, MD, MBA
physicians.institution: Cleveland Clinic — Rose Ella Burkhardt Brain Tumor & Neuro-Oncology Center
physicians.littFocus: Pioneer of stereotactic laser ablation (LITT) for brain tumors and radiation necrosis and an early adopter of the NeuroBlate system; long-standing leader in computer-assisted and stereotactic neurosurgery.

physicians.name: Alireza M. Mohammadi, MD
physicians.institution: Cleveland Clinic — Rose Ella Burkhardt Brain Tumor & Neuro-Oncology Center
physicians.littFocus: Leading investigator in LITT for gliomas and brain metastases; principal author on the multicenter LAANTERN NeuroBlate registry and on upfront-LITT studies in newly diagnosed glioblastoma.

physicians.name: Andrew E. Sloan, MD, MBA, FACS
physicians.institution: Affiliation in transition — recent sources conflict (Piedmont Healthcare, Atlanta vs. Premier Health / Wright State, Dayton); adjunct at Case Western Reserve
physicians.littFocus: Neurosurgical oncologist experienced in LITT for gliomas and metastases and in brain-tumor immunotherapy; formerly Director of the Brain Tumor & Neuro-Oncology Center at University Hospitals / Case Western in Cleveland.

physicians.name: Robert E. Gross, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Rutgers — Robert Wood Johnson & New Jersey Medical Schools (Chair of Neurosurgery)
physicians.littFocus: A principal developer and popularizer of stereotactic laser amygdalohippocampotomy (SLAH) for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy; leader in stereotactic laser ablation and DBS for epilepsy. Moved from Emory to Rutgers in 2023.

physicians.name: Jon T. Willie, MD, PhD, FAANS
physicians.institution: UT Health Austin / Dell Medical School, The University of Texas at Austin
physicians.littFocus: Major contributor to laser ablation for epilepsy, including SLAH outcomes and technique refinement; now Chief of Functional and Epilepsy Surgery at Dell Med after directing stereotactic/functional/epilepsy surgery at Washington University in St. Louis.

physicians.name: Michael R. Sperling, MD
physicians.institution: Thomas Jefferson University — Jefferson Comprehensive Epilepsy Center
physicians.littFocus: Epileptologist and Director of the Jefferson Comprehensive Epilepsy Center; the medical/epileptology counterpart in laser-ablation programs, contributing to selection and outcomes evidence for LITT/SLAH in drug-resistant epilepsy.

physicians.name: Peter E. Fecci, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (Chair of Neurosurgery; moved from Duke in 2025)
physicians.littFocus: National leader in combining LITT with immunotherapy for primary and metastatic brain tumors, including work on LITT-induced blood-brain-barrier disruption to enhance immune and drug delivery; previously directed the Duke Center for Brain and Spine Metastasis.

physicians.name: Eric C. Leuthardt, MD, MBA
physicians.institution: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis — Taylor Family Department of Neurosurgery
physicians.littFocus: Early adopter and investigator of LITT for gliomas and metastases and of LITT-mediated blood-brain-barrier disruption; broad innovator in brain-computer interfaces and neurotechnology.

physicians.name: Veronica L. Chiang, MD, FAANS
physicians.institution: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital (Director, Gamma Knife Center)
physicians.littFocus: Leading authority on LITT for brain metastases and post-radiosurgery radiation necrosis, including comparative work of LITT vs bevacizumab for radiation necrosis; integrates LITT with SRS in multidisciplinary brain-metastasis care.

physicians.name: Clark C. Chen, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University / Brown University Health (Director, Brain Tumor Program; moved from University of Minnesota in 2024)
physicians.littFocus: Neurosurgical oncologist focused on minimally invasive neuro-oncology including LITT for gliomas; NIH-funded glioblastoma researcher, formerly Chair of Neurosurgery at the University of Minnesota.

physicians.name: Nitin Tandon, MD
physicians.institution: McGovern Medical School, UTHealth Houston (Chief of Epilepsy Surgery)
physicians.littFocus: High-volume epilepsy surgeon who pioneered robot-assisted SEEG combined with MRI-guided laser ablation for drug-resistant epilepsy; leads the Texas Institute for Restorative Neurotechnologies.

physicians.name: Daniel J. Curry, MD
physicians.institution: Texas Children's Hospital / Baylor College of Medicine (Director, Functional Neurosurgery & Epilepsy Surgery)
physicians.littFocus: Pioneer of pediatric MRI-guided laser ablation for epilepsy (Texas Children's performed the world's first LITT-for-epilepsy case); particularly known for laser ablation of hypothalamic hamartomas and other pediatric epileptogenic lesions.

physicians.name: Ashwini D. Sharan, MD, FACS
physicians.institution: Thomas Jefferson University (Division Director, Functional & Epilepsy Neurosurgery)
physicians.littFocus: Leads Jefferson's surgical epilepsy program performing both ablative (laser) and resective procedures; past CNS president and a prominent figure in neuromodulation and minimally invasive epilepsy surgery.

physicians.name: Kris A. Smith, MD
physicians.institution: Barrow Neurological Institute — St. Joseph's Hospital & Medical Center
physicians.littFocus: Brain tumor and epilepsy surgeon who uses LITT for tumors and epilepsy; directs Barrow's Hypothalamic Hamartoma Program and Stereotactic-Functional-Epilepsy Fellowship, with laser ablation part of his minimally invasive practice.

physicians.name: Adrian W. Laxton, MD
physicians.institution: Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist / Wake Forest University School of Medicine (Director of Functional Neurosurgery)
physicians.littFocus: Functional and tumor neurosurgeon offering LITT/laser ablation for epilepsy and brain tumors alongside DBS and radiosurgery.

physicians.name: Sujit S. Prabhu, MD, FRCS
physicians.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center — Department of Neurosurgery
physicians.littFocus: High-volume LITT operator for deep-seated and eloquent gliomas and metastases; published widely on LITT for newly diagnosed and recurrent glioblastoma (including time-to-chemotherapy and IDH-wildtype outcomes) and involved in multicenter LITT efficacy work.

physicians.name: Dario J. Englot, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Vanderbilt University Medical Center (Surgical Director of Epilepsy)
physicians.littFocus: Surgical director of one of the country's highest-volume epilepsy programs; performs and studies laser ablation and SEEG for drug-resistant epilepsy, with a research focus on brain-network mechanisms of seizures and neuromodulation.
